items.title: ‘Why don’t you stay home?’: Muslim women in Kerala push back against Kanthapuram’s remarks
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Muslim women in Kerala are pushing back against the Grand Mufti of India, Kanthapuram AP Aboobacker Musliyar, after his remarks advocating restrictions on women’s participation in public life sparked widespread criticism on social media. Through videos and posts, women have challenged his views stating that such restrictions have no place in Kerala’s public life. The controversy began after the Kanthapuram-led faction of Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama recently issued a circular directing madrasas and local committees to bar women from public stages and prevent them from mixing with unrelated men at religious events. Defending the circular at a conference in Kochi, Kanthapuram said bringing women onto public platforms would lead to “great destruction” and argued that women should remain confined to their homes. His remarks triggered a wave of criticism, particularly from Muslim women and content creators on social media. Content creator Raseena Noushad criticised the idea that women’s role should be restricted to the home. “They believe women should stay at home, deliver babies, and cook,” she said.
